What Are the Key Requirements for an Application?

The application must include:

A clear description of the proposed activities

A detailed budget

A timeline for the funded activities

A plan for the long-term sustainability of the proposed society or network

A description of how the funded activities will lead to the establishment of a formal neuroscience community

The application should also demonstrate that the proposed activities are part of a genuine process toward establishment, rather than simply a one-off event.

What Is the Application Process?

Applicants must submit their application through the official IBRO Grants Portal.

The application window for the 2026 programme is:

1 September 2026 to 30 September 2026

The application deadline is therefore:

30 September 2026

Applications will be reviewed by an independent panel of experts.

Successful applicants will be notified by:

15 November 2026

The funded activities will then take place between:

1 January 2027 and 31 December 2027

The programme is designed to support the development of emerging neuroscience societies or thematic networks.

It is not intended to provide ongoing funding for established societies or networks.

The programme is particularly valuable where researchers are already interested in building a collaborative community but lack the financial resources needed to organize the planning process.

The IBRO Seeding Neuroscience Grants are intended to provide early-stage financial support for scientists who want to create stronger and more formal neuroscience communities.

The programme recognizes that in some countries or regions, neuroscientists may already be collaborating informally but lack:

A formal professional society

An organizational structure

Governance arrangements

A sustainable membership system

A dedicated regional chapter

A network focused on a particular neuroscience discipline

IBRO therefore provides funding for the inaugural activities needed to move from informal scientific collaboration toward a formal, sustainable structure.

This can include activities such as:

Governance planning

Strategic workshops

Organizational development

Discussions on leadership and membership

Planning the structure of a new neuroscience society

Developing a thematic scientific network

Establishing a regional or sub-national neuroscience chapter

The central purpose is not simply to organize another scientific event. Instead, the funding should help scientists create something that continues beyond the initial funded activity.

The programme is open to eligible initiatives in Africa, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
